questions.key_step: King property with $\frac1{1+5^x}$ on symmetric limits, after finding the intersection point.
questions.justification: Two stages (locate a, b from parabola and line, then the king trick) with a textbook trick; same trick as 2026-P2-Q4 plus a coordinate-geometry step.

questions.key_step: Rationalise with the constant difference of radicands, then two standard $\sqrt{x^2+a^2}$ integrals.
questions.justification: Routine chain of standard formulas with log simplification; no insight needed but several evaluation steps.

questions.key_step: Nested-log domain gives $(1,3)$; split $[x^2]$ at $\sqrt1,\sqrt2,\sqrt3$.
questions.justification: Two routine parts (domain, floor integral); options allow a check; far lighter than the 2021-P2-Q19 numerical greatest-integer integral.

questions.key_step: King property to remove $x$, then $\tan x=t$ on $[0,\pi/2]$.
questions.justification: King property plus a standard reduction to $1/(t^2+4)$: three linked routine moves, like the king-property anchors.

questions.key_step: Reflecting $x\to-x$ swaps $\sqrt{|x|-x}$ and $\sqrt{|x|+x}$, making the numerator a multiple of the denominator.
questions.justification: The surds with modulus hide the symmetry and need care with the sign of $x$; idea is less routine than the plain $1/(1+k^x)$ trick.

questions.key_step: Replace $x$ by $1/x$ and solve a $2\times2$ system; find the constant $g(1/2)$.
questions.justification: Standard functional-equation elimination followed by two easy integrals.

questions.key_step: King property turns $x+3$ into $\pi-x+3$; then $t=\cos x$.
questions.justification: Same pattern as 2026-P2-Q4 with a trigonometric integrand and an inverse-tangent finish.

questions.key_step: Substitute $2x=t$, then pair $t$ with $1-t$ because $t(1-t)$ is symmetric about $\frac12$.
questions.justification: Needs two moves (rescale, then king on a non-symmetric interval with an arbitrary $f$); a student must see that only $f(t(1-t))$ survives.

questions.key_step: Sign analysis of $t\sin t$ on each piece, then by parts.
questions.justification: Routine modulus integral with one by-parts; precision on signs only.

questions.key_step: Factor $f=(7t^6-3t^2)\sec^2x$, then by parts with $\tan^{-1}t$ and cancel $1+t^2$.
questions.justification: Hidden structure in $f$ and a by-parts whose algebra must cancel $1+t^2$; two linked ideas.

questions.key_step: Substitute $\ln x=t$ and apply $\frac{\phi(t)}{\phi(t)+\phi(6-t)}$.
questions.justification: One familiar form behind a log disguise; short once recognised.

questions.key_step: Write the Beta integral with $x=\sin^2\theta$ (or use $x+(1-x)=1$).
questions.justification: Single recognition step on a standard Beta identity.

questions.key_step: King property with $\frac1{1+e^x}$, then a by-parts integral of $x^2\cos2x$ and matching $\alpha,\beta$.
questions.justification: King trick plus a double chain (power reduction, by parts) and exact coefficient matching.

questions.key_step: Differentiate $g(x^3)$ and use $g'(x)=xf(x)$; sum an arithmetic series.
questions.justification: Routine Leibniz differentiation then a simple sum.

questions.key_step: Two by-parts steps linking $\int x^2F''$, $\int xF'$ and $\int F$.
questions.justification: Non-obvious chain of parts identities with boundary terms; one slip changes the final value.

questions.key_step: $f'(x)=x(x-4)(x-5)$ gives extrema; compare endpoint values.
questions.justification: Routine monotonicity and evaluation, with an endpoint comparison.

questions.key_step: Piecewise forms of $f(|x|)$ and $|f(x)|$, then integrate.
questions.justification: Careful piecewise casework but each step is elementary.

questions.key_step: King property turns $\frac{\cos\alpha x}{1+3^x}$ into $\int_0^1\cos\alpha x\,dx$; then solve $\sin\alpha/\alpha=2/\pi$.
questions.justification: One familiar trick followed by a check against the options; the final step is trial on options. Rated 2 because of the extra solving step.

questions.key_step: Three applications of L'Hopital (or a Maclaurin expansion) on $\int_0^xh/x^3$.
questions.justification: Routine but a few iterations or an expansion with cancellation of the linear term.

questions.key_step: Numerator $=\lambda D+\mu D'$ with $\lambda=12$, $\mu=-20$.
questions.justification: Standard linear-combination method followed by log simplification.
